collection: Synthetic teaching collection: peer tutoring and reading comprehension
notice: Every record in this file is invented for teaching. No study, author, journal or DOI here refers to real work. DOIs use the unassigned prefix 10.0000.

records.title: Peer tutoring and reading comprehension in Year 4: a cluster-randomised trial
records.abstract: We randomised 24 Year 4 classes in mainstream primary schools to a structured same-age peer tutoring programme or usual teaching for 12 weeks. Pupils worked in tutor-tutee pairs three times a week. Reading comprehension was measured with a standardised test. Classes using peer tutoring improved more than control classes (effect size 0.21).
records.planted: Straightforward eligible report: found by any reasonable strategy.

records.title: PEER TUTORING AND READING COMPREHENSION IN YEAR 4: A CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL
records.abstract: We randomised 24 Year 4 classes in mainstream primary schools to a structured same-age peer tutoring programme or usual teaching for 12 weeks. Pupils worked in tutor-tutee pairs three times a week. Reading comprehension was measured with a standardised test. Classes using peer tutoring improved more than control classes (effect size 0.21).
records.planted: Duplicate of R001 from a second database: different capitalisation, spelling (randomized), journal abbreviation and author format, and no DOI. A DOI-only deduplication misses it.

records.title: Peer tutoring improves comprehension: interim results from a Year 4 trial
records.abstract: Interim analysis of the first 14 classes in an ongoing cluster-randomised trial of same-age peer tutoring in Year 4. Comprehension scores rose more in tutoring classes. Final results are expected in 2019.
records.journal: Proceedings of the Synthetic Literacy Conference
records.planted: A second report of S01, not a duplicate record. Merging it with R001 as a duplicate would lose the link; it should be linked to the same study.

records.title: Reading buddies: older pupils as tutors for seven-year-olds
records.abstract: Year 6 pupils were trained to tutor Year 2 pupils in reading twice a week. Twelve schools took part; six started the scheme and six continued usual practice. Younger pupils in participating schools scored higher on a test of understanding what they had read.
records.planted: Eligible cross-age tutoring study that never uses the words peer or comprehension in title or abstract. A free-text block built on peer* and comprehension misses it; the Cross-Age Tutoring heading finds it.

records.title: Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies (PALS) for reading in Grades 2 and 3: trial registration
records.abstract: Planned randomised trial of Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies in 30 elementary classrooms. Primary outcome: reading comprehension at 20 weeks.
records.planted: Register record for S03. Not in either bibliographic database, so a database-only search cannot find it.

records.title: Effects of PALS on reading in the early elementary grades
records.abstract: Thirty elementary classrooms were randomly assigned to peer assisted learning or business as usual. Students in PALS classrooms made larger gains in passage comprehension than controls.
records.planted: Hyphenation and acronym variants: PALS, peer assisted, Peer-Assisted. A phrase search for "peer-assisted learning" in the title misses it; the title uses only the acronym.

records.title: Classwide tutoring by classmates and Grade 3 comprehension
records.planted: No abstract, and the title has tutoring and comprehension but neither peer nor reading. A free-text strategy that requires peer* or reading* misses it; the headings find it.

records.title: Same-age peer tutoring and reading comprehension in rural primary schools
records.abstract: Forty classes in rural primary schools were allocated by coin toss to peer tutoring or a comparison condition. Pupils aged 8 to 10 tutored each other in reading comprehension strategies. Comprehension improved more in tutoring classes.
records.planted: Indexing error: assigned Reading Fluency instead of Reading Comprehension, and no tutoring heading. A heading-only strategy misses it; free text finds it.

records.title: A pupil-led reading programme in Key Stage 2: a controlled evaluation
records.abstract: Pupils aged 7 to 11 in eight mainstream schools coached one another in reading for meaning, using a structured programme, while eight matched schools continued their usual programme. Pupils in programme schools showed greater gains in understanding of texts at the end of the year.
records.planted: Eligible, but the text says pupil-led, coached one another, reading for meaning and understanding of texts, with no peer, tutor* or comprehension in title or abstract. A free-text strategy built on those three terms misses it; the headings find it, and so does free text that adds coach*, one another and reading for meaning.

records.title: Peer tutoring for reading comprehension with Year 3 pupils: a randomised trial
records.abstract: Unlike earlier programmes developed in secondary schools, this trial tested a peer tutoring programme with Year 3 pupils in 18 primary schools. Schools were randomised to the programme or a waiting list. Reading comprehension improved more in programme schools.
records.planted: Mentions secondary schools in passing. A NOT "secondary school*" line, added to remove secondary-school studies, removes this eligible study.

records.title: Tutoring between equals and reading comprehension in Year 5 classrooms
records.abstract: This thesis reports a quasi-experimental study in which Year 5 pupils in six classes tutored each other in reading, compared with six classes receiving usual instruction. Comprehension outcomes favoured tutoring classes.
records.planted: Only in the theses index. Tutoring between equals is a literal translation of the Spanish term.

records.title: Tutoría entre iguales y comprensión lectora en quinto de primaria [Tutoring between equals and reading comprehension in the fifth year of primary school]
records.abstract: A quasi-experimental study in twelve fifth-year primary classes compared tutoring between equals with usual instruction. Reading comprehension improved more in the tutoring classes.
records.planted: Only in Database B. Non-English article with a translated title. Searching only Database A misses study S08 entirely.

records.title: Peer tutoring and reading comprehension in Year 5: a cluster-randomised replication
records.abstract: We replicated our Year 4 trial with a new sample of 22 Year 5 classes. Classes were randomised to structured peer tutoring or usual teaching. Reading comprehension improved more in tutoring classes (effect size 0.17).
records.planted: A different study with a title close to R001 and a shared first author. Fuzzy title matching at a loose threshold merges it with S01 and loses an eligible study.

records.title: Peer tutoring and reading comprehension in lower secondary school: a randomised trial
records.abstract: Students aged 12 to 14 in 20 secondary schools were randomised to peer tutoring or usual teaching. Reading comprehension improved slightly more in tutoring schools.
records.planted: Topically relevant; ineligible population (secondary school).

records.title: Volunteer reading tutors in primary schools: a randomised trial
records.abstract: Retired adult volunteers tutored Year 3 pupils in reading once a week. Twenty schools were randomised. Reading comprehension did not differ between groups.
records.planted: Ineligible intervention: tutors are adults, not pupils.

records.title: Peer tutoring in one primary school: comprehension before and after
records.abstract: Pupils in one primary school took part in peer tutoring for a term. Reading comprehension scores rose between the start and end of term. There was no comparison group.
records.planted: Ineligible design: single group, before and after.

records.title: Paired reading by classmates and oral reading fluency: a randomised trial
records.abstract: Year 2 classes were randomised to classmate paired reading or usual teaching. Oral reading fluency, in words read correctly per minute, improved more in paired-reading classes. Comprehension was not measured.
records.planted: Ineligible outcome: fluency only. The abstract contains comprehension, so it is retrieved and must be excluded at screening.

records.title: Peer tutoring and reading in primary schools: a systematic review
records.abstract: We reviewed controlled studies of peer tutoring for reading in primary schools and found small positive effects on comprehension.
records.planted: Not a primary study, so ineligible, but a seed for citation searching. Its reference list (see studies.csv) includes S02, S04 and S06.

records.title: Why peer tutoring deserves a second look

records.title: Peer tutoring in primary mathematics: a randomised trial
records.abstract: Year 4 pupils tutored each other in arithmetic. Twenty classes were randomised. Mathematics attainment improved more in tutoring classes; reading was not assessed.
records.planted: Ineligible outcome (mathematics). Retrieved by a peer tutoring and primary block that omits the reading concept.

records.title: Teacher-led small-group reading instruction and comprehension in Year 3
records.abstract: Year 3 classes were randomised to teacher-led small-group guided reading or whole-class teaching. Comprehension improved more with small groups.
records.planted: Ineligible intervention: teacher-led, not peer tutoring.

records.abstract: Pupils aged 7 to 11 in four special schools took part in peer tutoring for reading comprehension, compared with four schools continuing usual teaching.
